calls.video_title: Is Boeing an Undervalued Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now? | BA Stock Analysis
calls.price_at_call: $173 (stated current); DCF fair value $165; forward PE 80
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (first tracked) — down >20% YTD but still not a buying opportunity: fairly valued on DCF ($165 FV vs $173), expensive on forward PE 80, and execution risk remains as the 52-planes/month ramp slips to H2 2027.
calls.base_case: Revenue recovered to $94.9B (peak $102B in 2019); hitting 52/month in H2 2027 could push revenue past 2019 levels; FCF forecast $10B by 2028.
calls.bull_case: Hundreds of billions in backlog — no need to win new sales for years; debt down to ~$41B from $65B with $20B+ cash; cash flow improving.
calls.bear_case: Repeated deadline pushbacks — would not be surprised if the H2 2027 ramp slips again; thin margins (peak ~13% operating margin); EPS extremely volatile.

calls.video_title: 5 BEST STocks to BUY in November
calls.price_at_call: Down ~10% in the past week; still down 20% over 5 years
calls.thesis: BUY, first explicit Roussin BA call (prior note was UNCERTAIN watchlist only): a long-term cash-flow turnaround buy, explicitly not a next-month growth trade; owns it.
calls.base_case: Record order backlog at levels never seen, production ramping, and FCF turning positive through 2024-26 after the MAX grounding and pandemic years.
calls.bull_case: If Boeing converts the backlog efficiently, cash generation follows.
calls.bear_case: Execution, regulatory and financial-obligation risks; the path to stronger cash generation may take longer than investors expected.
